record.original_question: Does every triangulation of the torus admit a Grünbaum colouring, meaning a 3-edge-colouring in which each face sees all three colours?

evidence.quote: Question 5.3 Does every triangulation of the torus have a Grünbaum colouring?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $T$ be a triangulation of the torus, i.e., a simple graph embedded on the torus $S^1\times S^1$ so that every face is bounded by exactly three edges. A Grünbaum colouring of $T$ is an assignment $c:E(T)\to\{1,2,3\}$ of one of three colours to each edge such that for every face, the three edges on its boundary receive three distinct colours. 

Question: Does every triangulation of the torus admit a Grünbaum colouring?
artifact.status_search_result: Grünbaum's original conjecture (every simple triangulation of an orientable surface has a Grünbaum colouring) is known to be false in general — counterexamples exist on orientable surfaces of genus ≥ 5 — but it remains open for surfaces of genus 1 through 4. For the torus specifically, partial results are known: Albertson, Alpert, Belcastro and Haas (2010) proved that every triangulation $G$ of the torus with chromatic number $\chi(G)\neq 5$ admits a Grünbaum colouring, and Kotrbčík–Nakamoto–Noguchi–Ozeki–Vodopivec et al. showed every even triangulation of the torus has a Grünbaum colouring. The general question for arbitrary triangulations of the torus appears to still be open.

status_evidence.title: Grünbaum Colorings of Toroidal Triangulations
status_evidence.snippet: If G is a triangulation of the torus and χ(G) ≠ 5, then G has a Grünbaum coloring.
status_evidence.claim: Partial result resolving the toroidal case under a chromatic-number hypothesis.

status_evidence.title: Grünbaum colorings of even triangulations on surfaces
status_evidence.snippet: Every even triangulation on the projective plane, torus, or Klein bottle has a Grünbaum coloring.
status_evidence.claim: Resolution of the conjecture in the even-triangulation case on the torus.

status_evidence.title: Grünbaum coloring and its generalization to arbitrary surfaces
status_evidence.snippet: Grünbaum's conjecture is false for orientable surfaces of genus ≥ 5, but remains open for genus 1 to 4.
status_evidence.claim: Status of Grünbaum's conjecture across surfaces; torus case unresolved in general.
